DSC_4436-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 in Camping Paddock
DSC_4436-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A 2022 Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 in Chalk Grey metallic sits in a grass camping paddock at a motorsport event, parked alongside a bright yellow tunnel tent. The 718 Cayman GT4 is powered by a naturally aspirated 4.0-litre flat-six producing 420 hp, the same engine configuration used in the 718 Spyder. The UK registration plate LV22 XKP confirms this as a 2022-registered example.

DSC_4443-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Nissan GT-R, Lotus Emira and Porsche 911 Cabriolet at Track Day
DSC_4443-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: Three modern sports cars make their way along a paddock road at a UK track day event. In the foreground is a white Nissan GT-R (R35), followed by a blue Lotus Emira and a silver Porsche 911 (997-generation) Cabriolet with its roof down. The Nissan GT-R was developed by Nissan's GT-R development team under Kazutoshi Mizuno and launched in 2007, becoming renowned for its performance far exceeding its price point.

DSC_4452-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Nissan GT-R (R35) Rear View
DSC_4452-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A pearl white Nissan GT-R (R35) photographed from the rear at an outdoor car show, displaying UK registration plate D4 XDN. The twin circular LED tail lights and rear-mounted GT-R badge are clearly visible, along with the characteristic wide rear stance the R35 is known for. The R35 GT-R was produced from 2007 and earned a reputation for supercar-rivalling performance through its twin-turbocharged 3.8-litre V6 and advanced all-wheel-drive system.

DSC_4455-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Ferrari California on Show Field Display
DSC_4455-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A first-generation Ferrari California in Rosso Corsa is shown on static display at an outdoor automotive event. The California, introduced in 2008, was Ferrari's first front-engined V8 grand tourer and the first Ferrari to feature a retractable hardtop, combining open-air driving with everyday usability. The car is presented as a privately owned road car with no race livery, set against a busy show field of marquee tents and spectators.

DSC_4457-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Ferrari California and Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 on Display
DSC_4457-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A red Ferrari California and a silver Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 sit side by side on the grass at a car show, with a yellow event marquee in the background. The California, Ferrari's front-engined grand tourer introduced in 2008, was notable for being the first production Ferrari to feature a retractable hardtop roof. The Porsche wears a 2023 UK registration, indicating it is the current 718 Cayman GT4 generation.

DSC_4458-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Dodge Challenger Widebody with Ant Decal Livery
DSC_4458-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A dark grey Dodge Challenger Widebody on static display at an outdoor car show, instantly recognisable by its bold custom ant decals covering the rear quarter panels and boot lid. Orange brake calipers are visible through the dark multi-spoke wheels, a finishing detail consistent with the SRT Scat Pack and Hellcat Widebody variants. The wide rear haunches and spoiler highlight the Widebody's factory-flared bodywork, which adds 3.5 inches of track width over the standard Challenger.

DSC_4504-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: BMW M4 (F82) at Track Day Event
DSC_4504-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A red BMW M4 in F82 generation specification, registered ST17 RMW, pictured at a track day event with BMW M Performance branding on the windscreen. Behind it is a dark-coloured TVR, likely a Tuscan or Sagaris, adding to the performance car atmosphere of the occasion. The F82 M4 was introduced in 2014 as the successor to the E92 M3 coupe, marking the first time BMW applied the M4 name to the two-door body style.

DSC_4546-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 (992) with Le Mans 24h Livery on Static Display
DSC_4546-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A light grey Porsche 911 (992 generation) on static display at an outdoor car show, wearing door graphics commemorating the 24 Heures du Mans 2026 (10–14 juin 2026). The car carries XPEL paint protection film and Azuri Car Care sponsor branding, indicating it is a show or demonstration vehicle rather than an outright race entry. The 992-generation 911 was first introduced in 2019 and represents the eighth generation of Porsche's long-running sports car lineage.

DSC_4554-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Lamborghini Aventadors on Static Display
DSC_4554-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A pair of Lamborghini Aventadors — one in dark gunmetal grey and one in dark olive green — lined up on grass beneath a marquee tent at an outdoor car show. A red Toyota GR Supra is partially visible to the left. The Aventador's aggressive angular bodywork and wide rear diffuser are a hallmark of Lamborghini's naturally aspirated V12 flagship, which produces 690 hp in standard LP700-4 form.

DSC_4555-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 Carrera 4S Cabriolet
DSC_4555-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A silver Porsche 911 Carrera 4S Cabriolet photographed from the rear at an outdoor car show, Swiss-registered (canton Vaud). The 911 Carrera 4S distinguishes itself from the standard Carrera S with Porsche's all-wheel-drive system, widened rear bodywork, and larger brakes as standard. The quad exhaust outlets and characteristic engine lid louvres are clearly visible.

DSC_4558-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Lotus and Nissan GT-R NISMO at Car Show
DSC_4558-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A dark navy Lotus — identifiable by its distinctive louvred rear deck and the full "LOTUS" script across the tail panel — sits in the foreground at an outdoor enthusiast car show, with a white Nissan GT-R NISMO visible behind it. The GT-R features the NISMO's signature yellow brake calipers, black bonnet stripe, and red accent trim. Cars are displayed on grass in bright sunshine, typical of a concours or club gathering.

DSC_4560-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 GT2 RS (991.2) in GT Silver Metallic
DSC_4560-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A 991.2-generation Porsche 911 GT2 RS finished in GT Silver Metallic, photographed on static display at an outdoor automotive event. The car features the distinctive wide-body kit, large front air intakes, and forged magnesium wheels with yellow brake calipers. The 991.2 GT2 RS produces 700 hp from its twin-turbocharged 3.8-litre flat-six, making it the most powerful road-going 911 of its generation.

DSC_4563-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 GT2 RS (991.2) in GT Silver Metallic
DSC_4563-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A 2018 Porsche 911 GT2 RS (991.2) finished in GT Silver Metallic, photographed from the rear at an outdoor car show. The GT2 RS is the most powerful road-going 911 ever built at the time of its release, producing 700 PS from its twin-turbocharged 3.8-litre flat-six. The car is on static display alongside other performance vehicles, with a backdrop of white bell tents typical of UK automotive events.

DSC_4564-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Lotus Elise Series 2 on Display at Outdoor Car Show
DSC_4564-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A grey Lotus Elise Series 2 is pictured at an outdoor car show in France, parked alongside a Nissan 370Z. The Elise is a lightweight, mid-engined British sports car built around Lotus's signature aluminium tub chassis. The car carries 24 Heures du Mans event stickers on its windscreen and bonnet, consistent with an organised road-car gathering.

DSC_4572-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 in Racing Yellow
DSC_4572-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A Racing Yellow Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 on static display at a car show, photographed from the rear three-quarter angle. The GT4 is distinguished by its prominent fixed rear wing, dark multi-spoke alloys, and yellow-painted brake calipers. The 718 Cayman GT4 uses a naturally aspirated 4.0-litre flat-six engine producing 420 hp, shared with the 911 GT3.

DSC_4573-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Lamborghini Aventador on Static Display
DSC_4573-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A silver Lamborghini Aventador parked on grass at an outdoor car show event, surrounded by other vehicles. The Aventador, introduced in 2011 as the successor to the Murciélago, is powered by a naturally aspirated 6.5-litre V12 engine producing 700 hp. No race numbers or livery are present; this is a road car on static display.

DSC_4576-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 and BMW M340i at Car Show
DSC_4576-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A yellow Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 takes centre stage alongside a dark Aventurine Red BMW M340i at an outdoor UK car show, parked on grass in a mixed display of performance road cars. The Cayman GT4 is the track-focused variant of the mid-engined 718 Cayman, featuring a naturally aspirated flat-six engine, uprated suspension, and a rear wing — all carried over from the motorsport-derived GT programme. Both cars are shown on static display with UK registration plates.

DSC_4578-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 GT3 Touring (992) in Slate Grey
DSC_4578-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A Porsche 911 GT3 Touring in slate grey, finished with distinctive gold wheels, on static display at an outdoor car show. An orange and black cordon strap runs across the front bumper, part of the display barrier rather than the car itself. The 992-generation GT3 Touring omits the standard GT3's large rear wing in favour of a subtle integrated spoiler, making it one of the most subtle ways to access a naturally aspirated 510 hp flat-six. The event setting — grass field, white marquee tents in the background — suggests a concours or club display day.

DSC_4580-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 Targa (992) in Carmine Red
DSC_4580-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A Guards Red / Carmine Red Porsche 911 Targa, from the current 992 generation, on static display at an outdoor car show. The shot emphasises the car's distinctive Targa bar and signature round LED headlight, with a second 911 visible in the background. The 992 Targa revives Porsche's classic open-top format with an electrically retractable roof behind the fixed stainless-steel hoop, a feature first introduced on the original 911 Targa in 1967.

DSC_4583-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Audi R8 Coupe on Static Display
DSC_4583-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A Daytona Grey Audi R8 coupe (first generation, post-2012 facelift) on static display at an outdoor car show, registration R88 MHO. The car is finished with black multi-spoke alloy wheels and the R8's distinctive LED daytime running light strips that run the full width of each headlight cluster. The first-generation R8 was Audi's first mid-engined production road car, sharing its aluminium spaceframe platform with the Lamborghini Gallardo.

DSC_4585-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Audi R8 V8 at Car Show
DSC_4585-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A first-generation Audi R8 finished in matte dark grey queues at what appears to be an outdoor car show or concours event, identifiable by the white marquee tents in the background. The car wears UK registration R88 MHO and displays the R8 badge on the tail. The first-generation R8, introduced in 2007, was Audi's first mid-engined production supercar and shared its 4.2-litre V8 platform with the Lamborghini Gallardo.

DSC_4589-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Nissan GT-R Nismo on Static Display
DSC_4589-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A white Nissan GT-R Nismo, registration X011 FOX, photographed from the rear at an outdoor car show. The car carries an "LM 2026" decal featuring an RAF roundel on the rear quarter, alongside the prominent carbon fibre GT wing and GT-R badging. The Nismo variant of the R35 GT-R features aerodynamic and engine upgrades over the standard car, developed in collaboration with Nissan's motorsport division.

DSC_4590-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Audi RS3 Sportback with 24h Le Mans Livery
DSC_4590-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: An Audi RS3 Sportback (8Y generation) in Tango Red metallic on static display at an outdoor show, dressed in official 24 Heures du Mans branding including a windscreen banner, door graphics, and a Union Jack 24h Le Mans badge. The RS3 Sportback in this generation is powered by a 2.5-litre five-cylinder turbocharged engine producing 400 hp, a configuration Audi Sport has used in competition-derived road cars for over a decade. The car is parked on grass alongside a hospitality marquee, suggesting a motorsport event or manufacturer showcase setting.

DSC_4592-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 GT2 RS on Static Display
DSC_4592-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A 2018 Porsche 911 GT2 RS (991.2) in GT Silver Metallic with contrasting carbon fibre bonnet vents and a red interior, photographed on grass at an outdoor car show. The GT2 RS is the most powerful naturally road-legal 911 of its generation, producing 700 hp from its twin-turbocharged 3.8-litre flat-six. Yellow brake callipers and the wide-body stance mark it out as the range-topping RS variant.

DSC_4600-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Nissan GT-R Nismo on Static Display
DSC_4600-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A white Nissan GT-R Nismo (R35) on static display at an outdoor car show, finished with a black carbon-effect bonnet, red accent striping, and gold-centred black wheels. The car carries a 24 Heures du Mans door sticker and a UK registration plate. The GT-R Nismo is the most focused road-going variant of the R35, featuring uprated turbochargers and aerodynamic bodywork developed directly from Nissan's GT3 racing programme.

DSC_4601-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Nissan GT-R NISMO and Porsche 911 GT3 at Car Show
DSC_4601-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A white Nissan GT-R NISMO and a graphite grey Porsche 911 GT3 (992 generation) sit side by side on grass at an outdoor supercar gathering. The GT-R NISMO is distinguished by its red front splitter trim, a signature of the NISMO performance package developed in partnership with Nissan's motorsport division. The 992-generation GT3 alongside it features the model's characteristic large fixed rear wing and yellow brake calipers.

DSC_4606-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Paddock Scene at Motorsport Event
DSC_4606-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A person wearing a Prodrive-branded shirt and event accreditation lanyard poses in the paddock at a motorsport event. An Italian food vendor "La Dolce Vita" is visible in the background, its menu board advertising fresh Italian pizzas and puccia. The image does not feature a car or vehicle as its primary subject.

DSC_4612-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 944 with Martini-Style Livery
DSC_4612-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A red Porsche 944 wearing a Martini-inspired bonnet and roof stripe in red, white, and blue, registered G3OMAN, makes its way through the paddock at an outdoor car show or track day event. A black Porsche Cayenne follows closely behind. The 944, produced from 1982 to 1991, was notable for being the first Porsche to use a front-mounted, water-cooled four-cylinder engine developed entirely in-house.

DSC_4617-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 Carrera (964) in Guards Red
DSC_4617-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A Guards Red Porsche 911 Carrera of the 964 generation, registered in the UK in the 1990–1991 period, on static display at an outdoor motorsport or classic car event. The 964 was a significant evolution of the 911 line, introducing ABS, power steering, and a redesigned body that retained only around 15% of the previous 911's parts. The car sits on dark wheels against a backdrop of fellow enthusiasts and event marquees.

DSC_4619-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 (964) in Guards Red
DSC_4619-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A Guards Red Porsche 911 of the 964 generation (1989–1994) on static display at a car show. The 964 was the first 911 to feature all-wheel drive in the Carrera 4 variant, and introduced coil springs in place of the traditional torsion bars. This example rides on the period-correct black Porsche Cup design alloy wheels.

DSC_4621-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Porsche 911 (964) Carrera RS — 20th Anniversary Window Detail
DSC_4621-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A red Porsche 911 of the 964 generation, shown in static display at a car show. The quarter-window carries a commemorative shield sticker marking twenty years ("Zwanzig Jahre") of the 964 Carrera RS, dated 1992–2012. The 964-generation 911, produced from 1989 to 1994, was the first 911 to feature a fully integrated front and rear bumper design and introduced Porsche's all-wheel-drive Carrera 4 alongside the rear-wheel-drive Carrera 2.

DSC_4695-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR Pro on Static Display
DSC_4695-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: The Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR Pro, finished in a dark teal and black two-tone scheme, on static display at an indoor automotive event alongside what appears to be a Vantage GT3. Developed as a track-only evolution of the road-going Valkyrie, the AMR Pro produces over 1,000 bhp from its naturally aspirated Cosworth-developed V12 and generates enough downforce to theoretically corner at 3g. Pirelli P Zero slick tyres and the Aston Martin winged badge are clearly visible on the flanks.

DSC_4698-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Ford GT Mk IV — Pit Board Display
DSC_4698-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A Ford GT Mk IV on static display, shown alongside its illuminated Ford Racing pit identification board bearing the number 6:15. The car is finished in blue and rides on Michelin Pilot Sport tyres. The Ford GT Mk IV is a track-only race car developed by Ford Performance and Multimatic, built exclusively for competition rather than road use.

DSC_4699-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR Pro on Static Display
DSC_4699-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: The Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR Pro, finished in British Racing Green, photographed on static indoor display. Shod on Pirelli slick tyres, the car's extreme closed-wheel bodywork and aerodynamic side channelling distinguish the track-only AMR Pro variant from the road-going Valkyrie. The Valkyrie AMR Pro was designed to comply with Le Mans Hypercar regulations and produces over 1,000 bhp from its naturally aspirated Cosworth V12.

DSC_4700-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR Pro in British Racing Green — Indoor Show Display
DSC_4700-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A close-up study of the rear quarter of an Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR Pro finished in British Racing Green, shown on static indoor display at what appears to be a motor show or brand launch event. The car rides on Pirelli P Zero tyres with yellow lettering and features Akebono brake calipers behind multi-spoke black alloy wheels. The Valkyrie AMR Pro is a track-only evolution of the road-going Valkyrie hypercar, developed in collaboration with Red Bull Advanced Technologies and producing over 1,000 bhp from its naturally aspirated Cosworth V12.

DSC_4701-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: McLaren Racing Paddock Buggy at Le Mans
DSC_4701-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A McLaren Racing-liveried Club Car golf buggy photographed in the paddock, with Le Mans circuit signage visible in the background. The black utility cart carries official McLaren Racing branding and is numbered 01, used by the team for crew and equipment transport around the pit lane. A French-registered Iveco support truck is parked alongside, giving a glimpse of the logistical operation behind a top-tier endurance racing programme.

IMG_20260503_190752_005.jpg.title: Ferrari 512 TR
IMG_20260503_190752_005.jpg.caption: A red Ferrari 512 TR, registration ZV 12521, on display with the model designation clearly visible on its bodywork. The 512 TR succeeded the Testarossa in 1992; "TR" is itself an abbreviation of Testarossa, Italian for "red head" — a reference to the engine's distinctive red cam covers.

IMG_20260503_190904_828.jpg.title: Ferrari F40 — Wheel Detail
IMG_20260503_190904_828.jpg.caption: Detail of a Ferrari F40's front wheel arch — the five-spoke rim and Prancing Horse badge leave no doubt as to what you're looking at. The F40 was the last car personally approved by Enzo Ferrari before his death in August 1988 — the same year it was launched.

IMG_20260503_191325_342.jpg.title: Pagani Zonda
IMG_20260503_191325_342.jpg.caption: The rear of a Pagani Zonda in deep blue carbon-fibre, its quad exhaust pipes arranged with the kind of obsessive geometry that defines everything Horacio Pagani builds. On display courtesy of European Prestige. The Zonda takes its name from the warm, dry wind that sweeps across the Argentine Andes — a nod to founder Horacio Pagani's homeland.

IMG_20260503_191441_067.jpg.title: Porsche 911 — Le Mans Clubsport
IMG_20260503_191441_067.jpg.caption: A silver-white Porsche 911 bearing "Le Mans Clubsport" livery, registration ZV 35609, on display at the show.

IMG_20260503_191611_130.jpg.title: Porsche 911 Turbo 3.6 — Black and Silver
IMG_20260503_191611_130.jpg.caption: A black Porsche 911 Turbo 3.6 in the foreground, its "turbo 3.6" badging proudly on display, with a silver example behind. Both are unmistakably from the era when Porsche's turbo earned the nickname "widow-maker."

IMG_20260503_191840_818.jpg.title: McLaren Senna
IMG_20260503_191840_818.jpg.caption: A blue McLaren Senna on display, its carbon detailing and red brake callipers catching the light. Brutally functional aero, doors closed — this is a car built without apology. Named in honour of three-time Formula 1 World Champion Ayrton Senna, it was developed in close collaboration with the Senna family.

IMG_20260503_192032_018.jpg.title: Bentley — Custom Wrap
IMG_20260503_192032_018.jpg.caption: A pink Bentley wearing the irreverent slogans "UNLEADED IN HERE X" and "CAFFEINE BACK THERE" on its bodywork — a wry nod to the fuel that powers machine and crew alike.

IMG_20260503_192220_007.jpg.title: Ferrari F40
IMG_20260503_192220_007.jpg.caption: A red Ferrari F40 on display, its iconic lines unmistakable. The plate reads "40 RED." Appropriate. The F40 was the last car personally approved by Enzo Ferrari before his death in August 1988 — the same year it was launched.

IMG_20260503_192442_806.jpg.title: McLaren — Tail Detail
IMG_20260503_192442_806.jpg.caption: The tail of a grey McLaren at the show, Irish-registered with Sligo plates.

IMG_20260503_192712_783.jpg.title: Pagani Zonda — Front Three-Quarter
IMG_20260503_192712_783.jpg.caption: The same Pagani Zonda, now from the front three-quarter. Blue iridescent paint over exposed carbon-fibre, side strakes carving the air. A car from another dimension of coachbuilding. Every Zonda is powered by a Mercedes-AMG V12 — a partnership forged personally between Horacio Pagani and AMG.

IMG_20260503_234051_444.jpg.title: Porsche 911 GT3 RS
IMG_20260503_234051_444.jpg.caption: A Porsche GT3 RS in blue-grey, prepared by Custodian Classics in association with Porsche Centre Dublin, on display at the show.

IMG_20260503_234528_510.jpg.title: BMW M1
IMG_20260503_234528_510.jpg.caption: A white BMW M1 on display, wearing the full M-sport tricolour stripe the length of the car. Plate "H1 MZL." One of the rarest road cars BMW ever made. The M1 remains the only mid-engined production road car BMW has ever built.

IMG_20260503_234814_290.jpg.title: Two Early Porsche 911s
IMG_20260503_234814_290.jpg.caption: A dark green Porsche 911 in the foreground, a second example behind it — both from Custodian Classics, both wearing their age gracefully.

IMG_20260503_235252_421.jpg.title: Porsche 911 & Alfa Romeo Giulia
IMG_20260503_235252_421.jpg.caption: A silver early-generation Porsche 911 and a yellow Alfa Romeo Giulia GT, bearing the number 13181, share a frame at the show.

IMG_20260503_235536_754.jpg.title: Ferrari 275 GTB
IMG_20260503_235536_754.jpg.caption: A yellow Ferrari 275 GTB, registration ZV 7917, on display with its show placard confirming the 3285cc V12 beneath the bonnet. The 275 GTB was the first Ferrari road car to feature fully independent rear suspension on all four wheels.

IMG_20260504_000957_371.jpg.title: Alfa Romeo GTV
IMG_20260504_000957_371.jpg.caption: A red Alfa Romeo GTV, registration ZV 10818, the quad round headlights and shield badge centred in the frame.

IMG_20260504_001453_491.jpg.title: Alfa Romeo Giulia GT
IMG_20260504_001453_491.jpg.caption: A yellow Alfa Romeo Giulia GT, number 13181, front-on. Four round headlights, that unmistakable Alfa grille badge.

IMG_20260504_001721_116.jpg.title: Volkswagen New Beetle RSi
IMG_20260504_001721_116.jpg.caption: A Volkswagen New Beetle RSi with its bonnet propped open, the 3.2-litre VR6 on display under Deane Motor Company livery.

IMG_20260504_001947_200.jpg.title: Ford Transit Mk1
IMG_20260504_001947_200.jpg.caption: A red first-generation Ford Transit, front-on, the "FORD" lettering bold across the grille. A working man's icon among weekend dreamers.

IMG_20260504_002330_444.jpg.title: Porsche 911 (964) — J999 CUP
IMG_20260504_002330_444.jpg.caption: A yellow Porsche 911 (964 generation) carrying the plate "J999 CUP" on display at the show. The 964 was the first 911 to offer all-wheel drive as a production option, introduced with the Carrera 4 in 1989.

IMG_20260504_002654_112.jpg.title: Porsche 911 Turbo (930) — Rear
IMG_20260504_002654_112.jpg.caption: The rear of a silver Porsche 911 Turbo (930) under the Custodian Classics banner, whale-tail spoiler and "turbo" script on the engine lid.

IMG_20260504_003126_589.webp.title: Pagani Zonda — Diffuser Detail
IMG_20260504_003126_589.webp.caption: Close-up of the Pagani Zonda's rear diffuser and exhaust arrangement. The chrome "Zonda" script sits above the carbon-fibre mesh, blue iridescent paint glowing behind it. The Zonda was the first car produced by Pagani Automobili, entering production in 1999.

DSC_4855-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Cadillac V-Series.R #38 — Le Mans 2026
DSC_4855-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: The No. 38 Cadillac Racing entry, backed by Hertz, in the pit lane at Le Mans 2026.

DSC_4870-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Corvette Z06 GT3.R #33 — Le Mans 2026
DSC_4870-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: The yellow No. 33 Keating entry on Goodyear rubber during the WEC 24-hour race, its vivid livery standing out as the endurance battle unfolds.

DSC_4871-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Keating Motorsport Corvette #33 — Le Mans 2026
DSC_4871-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: The yellow Keating machine in the pit lane, Rolex and Motul signage overhead — Le Mans at full nocturnal intensity.

DSC_4875-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR Pro #007 — Le Mans 2026
DSC_4875-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: A dark green Aston Martin running under The Heart of Racing banner in the pit lane at Le Mans 2026. The Valkyrie road car uses a Cosworth-developed 6.5-litre naturally aspirated V12 that revs beyond 11,100 rpm — one of the highest-revving engines ever fitted to a production road car.

DSC_4876-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Aston Martin Thor Team — Le Mans 2026
DSC_4876-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: The dark green No. 007 Aston Martin of the Thor Team, carrying the Heart of Racing banner, in the pit complex at Le Mans 2026.

DSC_4879-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Michelin Chicane — 24h Le Mans 2026
DSC_4879-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: The Michelin chicane arch at night, lit up with "24h Le Mans 10–14 Juin 2026" signage. Taillights trace through the dark in the distance.

DSC_4881-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Ford Racing #88 — Le Mans 2026
DSC_4881-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: The blue No. 88 Ford Racing machine in the pit lane at Le Mans 2026, its livery unmistakable under the racing lights.

DSC_4891-Enhanced-NR.jpg.title: Le Mans at Night — Circuit de la Sarthe
DSC_4891-Enhanced-NR.jpg.caption: Michelin and Rolex branding frame the action at the 24 Heures du Mans 2026. The circuit atmosphere captures the prestige that defines the legendary race.
